rot.finalNet.ideia.canto.e1: Attack: your bishop is light-squared, like the a8 and h1 corners: these are the corners of the bishop's colour. Only there can the bishop check the king in the corner; in the other two, dark corners, it never reaches it.
rot.finalNet.ideia.canto.e2: For the mate, the three pieces build the mating net: they take every square from the black king, and one of them gives check. Here the king covers b6, b7 and b8, and the bishop covers a6. Only a7 and a8 remain.
rot.finalNet.ideia.canto.l1: The knight checks from c8 and takes a7. The black king is left with a8 only, precisely the corner of the bishop's colour.
rot.finalNet.ideia.canto.l2: The black king goes to a8, its only square. Note: the bishop reaches the a8 diagonal in one move.
rot.finalNet.ideia.canto.l3: The bishop checks along the long diagonal, and the black king has no square: mate. The king covers b7 and b8, the knight covers a7, and the bishop gives check.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.e1: Attack: the black king is trapped on a8, and its only way out is to capture the unprotected knight on b8. How do you protect the knight without stalemating the black king?
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.certo: On c7, the king protects the knight and leaves a7 free: the black king gains a square, and there is no stalemate.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.revela: The move is the king to c7: it protects the knight and leaves a7 free for the black king, with no stalemate.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.fora: That move is not one of those we are studying here. Let us go back to the position.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.volta: Let us go back to the position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.err.b8c6.1: With this move, the knight leaves b8, but from c6 it covers a7 and b8: the black king is stalemated, a draw.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.err.b8d7.1: With this move, the knight covers b8 from d7, and the white king already covers a7 and b7: the black king is stalemated, a draw.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.err.a6b7.1: With this check, the bishop on b7 is protected by the king, but the knight on b8 is still unprotected.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.err.a6b7.2: Black captures the knight on b8: a draw.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.l1: Now the plan: the bishop will give check on b7, protected by the king, and the knight will deliver the mate.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.l2: The black king goes to a7, the square it has just gained.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.l3: The bishop goes to c8 and prepares the check on b7, a square protected by your king. On b7 now, the bishop would stalemate the black king.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.l4: The black king goes back to a8, its only square: the knight watches a6, and your king b6, b7 and b8.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.l5: The bishop checks from b7, protected by the king, and takes a6. The black king only has a7.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.l6: The black king goes to a7, the last free square.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.l7: The knight mates from c6. The bishop takes a6 and a8, and the king takes b6 and b8: the mate comes on a7, next to the corner of the bishop's colour.
rot.finalNet.ideia.protecao.l8: Remember: in the mating net, every piece stays protected, and the black king always has a move until the final check. Without that, it is a capture or stalemate.
rot.finalNet.demos.escuro.e1: Attack: now the bishop is dark-squared, and the black king is on h8, the corner of the bishop's colour. It only has g8: watch out for stalemate.
rot.finalNet.demos.escuro.l1: The bishop goes to c5 and takes f8, without touching g8: the black king still has a move.
rot.finalNet.demos.escuro.l2: The black king goes to g8, its only square.
rot.finalNet.demos.escuro.l3: The knight checks from h6. With f8 covered by the bishop, the black king can only go back to h8.
rot.finalNet.demos.escuro.l4: The black king goes back to h8, its only square.
rot.finalNet.demos.escuro.l5: The bishop mates along the long diagonal: the king covers g7 and h7, the knight covers g8.
rot.finalNet.demos.cavalo.e1: Attack: the bishop is light-squared, and the black king is next to h1, the corner of the bishop's colour. This time, the knight gives the mate.
rot.finalNet.demos.cavalo.l1: The king goes to f2 and takes g1, g2 and g3. The black king is left with h1 only, because the bishop watches h3.
rot.finalNet.demos.cavalo.l2: The black king goes to h1, its only square.
rot.finalNet.demos.cavalo.l3: The bishop checks from g2, protected by the king, and takes h3. The black king can only go back to h2.
rot.finalNet.demos.cavalo.l4: The black king goes back to h2, its only square.
rot.finalNet.demos.cavalo.l5: The knight mates from f3. The bishop covers h1 and h3, and the king covers g1 and g3: the same net, with the knight's check.
rot.finalNet.pratica.escuroA1.p: Play White and mate in the corner of your bishop's colour. Keep your pieces protected and always leave the black king a move.
rot.finalNet.pratica.escuroA1.fim: Mate in the corner of the bishop's colour: the pieces protected, and the black king with a move until the final check.
rot.finalNet.pratica.escuroA1.fins.afoga: The black king is stalemated: a draw. Always leave a free square until the mate.
rot.finalNet.pratica.escuroA1.fins.repet: The same position occurred three times: a draw. Tighten the net with every move, without going back.
rot.finalNet.pratica.escuroA1.fins.limit: The move limit ran out before the mate. Close the net with the king, knight and bishop together.
rot.finalNet.pratica.escuroA1.fins.insuf: Insufficient material is left for mate: a draw. Keep the bishop and knight protected.
